claims.text: Optimizing HVOF spraying distance and oxygen partial pressure will promote controlled in situ formation of protective oxide phases in a FeNiCoCrMo0.5Al1.3 coating.
The controlled protective oxide phases will enhance the coating's resistance to high-temperature oxidation.
The optimized coating will retain the zirconium-alloy cladding's suitability for service.
Controlled in-flight oxidation will produce a refined, supersaturated BCC solid-solution microstructure.
The coating will contain uniformly distributed, pre-formed protective oxide particles.
The pre-formed protective oxide particles may include alpha-Al2O3.
Precise control of HVOF parameters induces limited oxidation of the feedstock during flight.
Limited in-flight oxidation forms stable oxide phases within the deposited coating.
Pre-formed oxide phases act as a barrier to oxygen ingress during subsequent high-temperature exposure.
Reduced oxygen ingress will suppress further coating oxidation and protect the zirconium-alloy substrate.
Relative to standard HVOF coatings or uncoated cladding, the optimized coating will have lower oxidation penetration.
Relative to standard HVOF coatings or uncoated cladding, the optimized coating will have lower oxide weight gain.
The optimized coating will exhibit an enhanced microhardness profile under high-temperature conditions.
The optimized coating will maintain mechanical integrity under the tested conditions.
The protective effect is expected at approximately 800 °C in both static and dynamic oxidizing atmospheres.
Performance under extreme accident scenarios and long-term reactor operation has not been validated.
